CSE-05-cse0-setup-and-tooling/README.md.content:
# CSE0: C17 setup and diagnostic evidence

This required project establishes a repeatable build, test, debugger, and
sanitizer workflow. The small reading classifier keeps the algorithm visible:
values below 0 map to -1, values from 0 through 100 map to 0, and values above
100 map to 1. No arithmetic is needed, including at INT_MIN and INT_MAX.

## Read the source before building

`reading.h` declares the contract. `main.c` defines the function and prints a
five-reading trace. `tests.c` checks nine independent fixtures. In the learner
folder only the body of `classify_reading` needs completion; preserve the public
signature, driver, and tests. The reference implements the same contract.
An untouched learner builds, then exits 78 with an unfinished-work message.
Its contract test fails. A successful compiler invocation does not establish
correct behavior.

For value 100 the first comparison is false and the second comparison is also
false, so the result is 0. Changing `> 100` to `>= 100` is a controlled
regression: the value-100 fixture must reject it.

## Native setup and first run

Use a Clang or GCC C17 compiler, CMake 3.20 or newer, and LLDB or GDB. On macOS,
Apple command-line tools supply Clang and LLDB. A Unix-style terminal is also
available in Windows through WSL2. Record each installed tool's version.
The site editor can store source; native compilation and diagnostics require
the local toolchain described here.

From the learner folder:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/cse0_starter
```

The last two commands initially fail as described above. Complete the named
function and repeat both commands. From the reference folder the corresponding
commands are:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/cse0_solution
```

Both roles enforce C17 and `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`. The complete trace
is:

```text
-1 => -1
0 => 0
50 => 0
100 => 0
101 => 1
```

The tests cover INT_MIN, -1, 0, 1, 50, 99, 100, 101, and INT_MAX. Explain why
those fixtures exercise both boundaries and all three categories. Predict one
additional case, add it without removing existing fixtures, and check it.

## Diagnostic and debugger pass

Build the completed role with address and undefined-behavior diagnostics:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-sanitized -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON
cmake --build build-sanitized
ctest --test-dir build-sanitized --output-on-failure
```

`unsafe_probe.c` is a separate, deliberately invalid fixture outside normal
builds. From `CSE-05-cse0-setup-and-tooling` (one level above either role), compile
and run it in isolation:

```sh
clang -std=c17 -g -O0 -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer unsafe_probe.c -o build-unsafe-probe
./build-unsafe-probe
```

It indexes element 4 in a four-element array. The diagnostic must reject the
run and identify the invalid access. Do not treat its failure as a successful
application run. The corrected classifier remains a separate clean program.

Open the completed executable in LLDB or GDB, set a breakpoint in
`classify_reading`, run it, inspect `value`, and step through the comparisons.
Record one observation connecting source, state, and the printed result.

## Completion and walkthrough

Submit tool versions, clean build/test output, the five-line trace, a diagnosed
unsafe fixture, a clean sanitized classifier run, and a test that rejects the
controlled boundary regression. A student can follow this sequence alone;
with an instructor, compare predictions before each run and use diagnostic
output to explain the correction. The notebook is evidence, not another
implementation of the same helper. Reference comparison follows a saved
learner attempt.

CSE-05-cse0-setup-and-tooling/starter/CM.content:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(cse0_starter C)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS OFF)
option(CSE_SANITIZERS "Build this pack with address/undefined diagnostics" OFF)

add_executable(cse0_starter main.c)
add_executable(cse0_starter_tests tests.c main.c)
target_compile_definitions(cse0_starter_tests PRIVATE CSE_NO_MAIN)
foreach(target cse0_starter cse0_starter_tests)
    if(CMAKE_C_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang|GNU")
        target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror)
        if(CSE_SANITIZERS)
            target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer)
            target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE -fsanitize=address,undefined)
        endif()
    else()
        message(FATAL_ERROR "Use a Clang or GCC C17 toolchain for this pack")
    endif()
endforeach()

# Unfinished learner checks are useful locally but are not a root acceptance gate.
if(CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR STREQUAL CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR OR FALSE)
    enable_testing()
    add_test(NAME cse0_starter_contract COMMAND cse0_starter_tests)
endif()

CSE-06-unit-1-why-c-for-systems-work/REA.content:
# Unit 1: translation units and linking

This required project deliberately reuses the completed setup classifier's
behavior. The new goal is its build structure: separate translation units,
header declarations, object files, and the linker. Reimplementing the previous
algorithm is not the requirement.

## Files and contract

- `reading.h`: declarations shared by all source files; its include guard
  prevents repeated declarations within one translation unit.
- `reading.c`: the provided classifier from setup.
- `labels.c`: the learner task. Implement `reading_label`: categories -1, 0,
  and 1 produce `below`, `within`, and `above`; every other category produces
  `invalid`. Return pointers to string literals; callers do not free them.
- `main.c`: the unchanged driver connecting both functions.
- `tests.c`: six label fixtures plus four cases spanning both source files.

The starter builds but its label helper returns NULL, so its driver exits 78
and its tests fail safely. Complete only that helper. Compare with the separate
reference after saving an attempt. Both folders build independently.

## Clean build and expected trace

From the learner folder:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/cse1_link_starter
```

Before completion the test and program commands fail. From the reference folder:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/cse1_link_solution
```

The complete trace is:

```text
-1 => below
0 => within
50 => within
100 => within
101 => above
```

For value 101, `reading.c` returns category 1. `main.c` passes that category to
`labels.c`, obtains the literal `above`, and prints it. The declaration lets
`main.c` compile before the linker connects those definitions.

## Observe the source-to-program boundary

Run these commands from a completed role. Preprocessed source includes the
header text; assembly represents generated instructions; an object file has
compiled code plus symbol information but has not been linked into this
program.

```sh
cc -std=c17 -E main.c -o main.i
cc -std=c17 -S main.c -o main.s
cc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -c main.c reading.c labels.c
nm main.o reading.o labels.o
cc main.o reading.o labels.o -o linked-reading
./linked-reading
```

Inspect the undefined references in `main.o` and the definitions in the other
objects. Symbol decoration varies by platform, so explain the relationship
rather than copying an exact `nm` spelling.

These two controlled link commands must fail:

```sh
cc main.o reading.o -o missing-label-definition
cc main.o reading.o labels.o labels.o -o duplicate-label-definition
```

The first omits the object defining `reading_label`. The second supplies that
definition twice. Compile each source once and use the successful link command
to recover. Header guards act during preprocessing; they do not resolve
multiple external definitions in different translation units.

## Check and explain

The label tests cover -1, 0, 1, INT_MIN, 2, and INT_MAX. The cross-file tests
cover readings -1, 0, 100, and 101. Add a new outside-range category and one new
within-range reading after predicting their results. Preserve existing tests.
Use `-DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON` in a separate CMake build for a clean diagnostic pass.

Completion includes the clean trace, passing fixtures, one preprocessed or
assembly observation, symbol evidence, both expected link failures, and a
successful clean rebuild. For an instructor walkthrough, predict each failure
before running it; independently, write the prediction first and compare the
actual message afterward. Source editing and native build evidence are
separate parts of the workflow.

CSE-07-unit-8-function-pointers-and-disp.content:
# Unit 8: Function Pointers and Dispatch

This required project implements a small command dispatcher in C17. A command
name selects a function from a table, and that function changes a device state.
The table is data: the dispatcher must work with caller-supplied handlers as
well as the three provided commands. This makes indirect calls observable.

Use `starter` for the learner attempt. `solution` is a separate reference for
comparison after saving an attempt. Both roles contain their own CMake build,
driver, header, handlers and tests. Clang or GCC and CMake 3.20 or newer must
already be installed. This project installs no tools.

## Read the types before implementing the dispatcher

Prerequisites are arrays, structs, strings, pointer arguments, and the header /
translation-unit distinction from Unit 1. `DeviceState.level` is an integer from
0 through 100, inclusive. `CommandStatus` describes a result independently of
that state.

In `dispatch.h`, this declaration names a pointer to a function:

```c
typedef CommandStatus (*CommandHandler)(DeviceState* state, int argument);
```

The parentheses around `*CommandHandler` make this a function-pointer type.
Every handler accepts the same two arguments and returns the same enum type.
A `CommandEntry` stores a command name together with one such pointer. The
expression `entries[i].handler(state, argument)` calls the stored function;
the dispatcher does not need to know its implementation. Do not cast between
data pointers and function pointers or invent a different signature.

Read `handlers.c` and trace `store`, `take` and `clear` through
`builtin_commands`. The command names are case-sensitive. `strcmp(a, b) == 0`
means the complete strings match, so `storex` does not match `store`.

## Required contract

Complete only `dispatch_command` in `starter/dispatch.c`. Keep the supplied
handlers, public API, driver and 31 checks unchanged.

1. Reject a null state, null command, or state level outside 0 through 100 with
   `COMMAND_BAD_ARGUMENT` before calling any handler.
2. A nonempty table requires a non-null table pointer. Every entry must have a
   non-null name and handler. Validate the entire table before invoking a
   callback; a malformed later entry must not allow an earlier callback to run.
3. An empty table is valid, including `(NULL, 0)`, and returns `COMMAND_UNKNOWN`.
4. Select the first entry whose complete name matches the command. Duplicate
   names therefore select the earlier entry. Call exactly that stored handler
   once, with the original state pointer and unchanged integer argument.
   Return its status. Do not hard-code the three built-in command names.
5. If no name matches, return `COMMAND_UNKNOWN` without calling a handler or
   changing the state. Validation and lookup failures preserve state.

The caller supplies live storage for `count` entries and valid, terminated
name strings. The table and strings remain alive throughout the call. A
callback owns its behavior; the dispatcher passes through its result. The
provided handlers retain the level on every unsuccessful command:

| Command | Argument | Success | Failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `store` | 1 through 100 | Add to the level | `full` if capacity would be exceeded |
| `take` | 1 through 100 | Subtract from the level | `empty` if insufficient level remains |
| `clear` | exactly 0 | Set the level to 0 | Other arguments are invalid |

An argument outside the specified range returns `bad-argument` before a
capacity or availability check. These small bounds keep arithmetic defined,
including when callers pass `INT_MIN` or `INT_MAX`.

## Build, test and run

Download the selected role folder and this guide, or clone the repository.
From this project directory, choose the learner role:

These commands use a POSIX shell on macOS, Linux, or WSL. Use the Clang/GCC
toolchain configured during setup.

```sh
cd starter
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/cse8_dispatch_starter
```

The untouched learner compiles cleanly, but its tests fail and its driver exits
78 with an unfinished/incorrect-dispatch message. It must not be mistaken for
a completed program because it builds. A correct attempt reports
`31 dispatch checks passed`; CTest passes and the driver exits 0 with:

```text
store(4): ok, level=4
take(2): ok, level=2
store(99): full, level=2
clear(0): ok, level=0
unknown(0): unknown, level=0
```

The reference uses the same sequence from `solution`, with executable
`./build/cse8_dispatch_solution`. Keep learner and reference build directories
separate. CMake selects `main.c` for the driver and `tests.c` for the tests;
compiling all `.c` files into one program would introduce two `main` functions.

For address and undefined-behavior diagnostics, configure a separate build:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-sanitized -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON
cmake --build build-sanitized
ctest --test-dir build-sanitized --output-on-failure
```

Use a debugger with the normal Debug build. For example, start
`lldb ./build/cse8_dispatch_starter`, set `breakpoint set --name
dispatch_command`, and `run`. Inspect the command, argument, table entry and
level, then step to the selected handler. A GCC/GDB setup can use
`gdb ./build/cse8_dispatch_starter`, `break dispatch_command`, and `run`.
Do not edit the driver or suppress a failing test to produce the expected trace.

## Completion evidence and instructor walkthrough

Save the source attempt, the passing CTest output, the five-line trace, and one
debugger observation identifying the chosen table entry and callback. Explain
why `storex` is unknown, why a full device keeps its earlier level, and why the
caller-supplied `observe` handler in `tests.c` works without changing dispatch.

For a walkthrough, first predict each driver transition, then trace one table
lookup together. The learner implements the lookup, tests custom-table and
failure cases, and explains the observed indirect call. This same sequence can
be followed independently. Compare the reference only after preserving the
attempt, and explain differences rather than replacing files wholesale.

Optional extension: add a new handler and table entry in a separate copy, then
add tests for its state rule. The existing dispatcher should accept it without
adding another hard-coded branch. Keep this extension separate from the
required 31-check completion contract.

CSE-08-unit-10-engineering-math-in-code/.content:
# Unit 10: Engineering Math in Code

This required C17 project converts three engineering quantities with scaled
integers. The same stored integer has a meaning only when its unit and scale
are specified. For example, `2500` centi-C means 25.00 degrees Celsius, while
`2500` microseconds means 0.002500 seconds.

Prerequisites are integer types, functions, pointer output arguments, and the
header/source/build distinction from Unit 1. Read `engineering_math.h`, the
supplied voltage conversion in `engineering_math.c`, and the three driver
calls in `main.c`. A Clang or GCC C17 compiler and CMake 3.20 or newer must
already be installed. This project installs no tools.

Use `starter` for the learner attempt. Complete only the two marked functions
in `starter/engineering_math.c`. Preserve the header, voltage conversion,
driver, and 52 expectations in `tests.c`. `solution` is an independent
reference build; compare it after preserving the learner attempt.

## Units, formulas, and rounding

No function uses floating point. Each successful function stores its result
through an output pointer and returns `MATH_OK`. Invalid parameters return
`MATH_BAD_ARGUMENT`. A result outside the output type returns `MATH_OVERFLOW`.
Every failure leaves a non-null output unchanged; a null output is invalid.

| Function | Inputs | Stored result | Rounding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `celsius_to_fahrenheit` | Signed centi-C (`int32_t`) | Signed centi-F (`int32_t`) | Truncate the scaled term toward zero |
| `adc_to_millivolts` | ADC sample, full-scale count, reference mV (`uint32_t`) | mV (`uint32_t`) | Nearest mV; exact halves round upward |
| `duration_to_ticks` | Duration in microseconds, clock frequency in Hz (`uint32_t`) | Whole ticks (`uint32_t`) | Round upward so the requested delay is not shortened |

### Temperature: preserve the fraction until division

The familiar formula is F = C × 9 / 5 + 32. For centi-units, calculate
`truncate_toward_zero(centi_C * 9 / 5) + 3200`. C17 signed integer division
truncates toward zero: `9 / 5` is 1 and `-9 / 5` is -1. Cast an operand to
`int64_t` **before** multiplying, then divide and add in that wider type.
Casting an already overflowed product does not repair it.

The entire `int32_t` input range times 9 fits `int64_t`. The final value still
needs a check against `INT32_MIN` and `INT32_MAX` before storing it. Converting
`INT32_MAX` or `INT32_MIN` is an overflow result, rather than a physically
meaningful temperature. These extreme cases make range handling observable.
`1193044693` and `-1193048249` are the last accepted inputs at the upper and
lower result boundaries; the adjacent inputs must fail without changing the
output.

The scaled term's truncation error is less than one centi-F (0.01 degree F).
Negative values expose a common error: dividing the input by 5 first loses
information. `-1` centi-C converts to `3199` centi-F, not `3200`.

### Voltage: read the supplied implementation

For a linear ADC, the ideal result is `sample * reference_mV / full_scale`.
`full_scale` and `reference_mV` must be positive, and `sample <= full_scale`.
This exercise assumes the stated linear model; it does not account for a
physical sensor's calibration, noise, or tolerances.

The supplied function multiplies in `uint64_t`, computes quotient and
remainder, and rounds upward when the remainder is at least half of the
denominator. `(denominator + 1) / 2` handles both even and odd denominators
without doubling a large remainder. The maximum `uint32_t` product fits
`uint64_t`, and the valid sample range keeps the rounded output at or below
`reference_mV`, so the result fits `uint32_t`. The rounding error is at most
0.5 mV. Explain why 512/1023 of 3300 mV becomes 1652 mV, and why half of 1 mV
rounds to 1 mV.

### Timing: round upward and check the result

Calculate the ideal ticks as `duration_us * frequency_hz / 1000000`, with a
`uint64_t` multiplication before division. For positive frequency, zero
duration is valid and produces zero ticks. Zero frequency is invalid.
Divide first, then add one tick exactly when a remainder remains. This avoids
adding a rounding offset to the original product. Check against `UINT32_MAX`
before storing.

The stored count is never less than the ideal count and is less than one tick
above it. At 1000 Hz, 1501 microseconds requires 2 ticks. This is a numeric
conversion contract, not a promise about operating-system scheduling or an
actual hardware timer's latency.

## Build, test, and inspect

Download the selected role and this guide, or clone the repository. From the
project directory, choose the learner role. These commands use a POSIX shell
on macOS, Linux, or WSL:

```sh
cd starter
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
./build/cse10_math_starter
```

The untouched learner compiles, but its checks fail and the driver exits 78
with an unfinished/incorrect-conversion message. A correct attempt reports
`52 engineering math checks passed`; CTest succeeds and the driver exits 0:

```text
temperature: -4000 centi-C -> -4000 centi-F
voltage: 512/1023 at 3300 mV -> 1652 mV
timer: 1501 us at 1000 Hz -> 2 ticks
```

The reference uses the same commands in `solution`, with executable
`./build/cse10_math_solution`. Keep role build directories separate. The
driver and tests each define `main`, so use the provided CMake targets rather
than compiling all `.c` files into one executable.

Enable address and undefined-behavior diagnostics in a separate build:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-sanitized -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON
cmake --build build-sanitized
ctest --test-dir build-sanitized --output-on-failure
```

With the normal Debug build, use `lldb ./build/cse10_math_starter` and set
`breakpoint set --name duration_to_ticks`, or use
`gdb ./build/cse10_math_starter` and `break duration_to_ticks`. Run and inspect
the widened product, quotient, remainder, and output before assignment.

## Completion evidence and instructor walkthrough

Predict a negative temperature case, a voltage tie, a fractional timer case,
and an overflow before implementing the two functions. Implement, run all

CSE-09-unit-11-systems-tooling/README.md.content:
# Unit 11: Systems Tooling

This required project applies compiler, linker, sanitizer, debugger, and binary
inspection tools to the temperature/voltage/timer utility from Unit 10. Its
conversion contract and 52 checks remain the same. The learner diagnoses three
localized faults in a familiar program rather than implementing a new formula.
The reference uses the accepted conversion functions unchanged.

Prerequisites are Unit 1's translation-unit model and Unit 10's fixed units,
rounding, widened arithmetic, and output-range rules. Read `engineering_math.h`,
the two TODO comments in `engineering_math.c`, the TODO in `main.c`, and
`tests.c`. Do not change the public API, expected values, or warning policy.

Clang or GCC with C17 support, CMake 3.20+, a debugger (GDB or LLDB), and binary
inspection tools (`nm` plus `objdump` or `llvm-objdump`) must already be
installed. These instructions use a POSIX shell on macOS, Linux, or WSL.
Tool installation is part of setup; this pack installs nothing.

## Keep diagnosis and repair separate

Use `starter` for the learner attempt. Unlike earlier learners, its initial
strict build intentionally fails. Do not disable `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic
-Werror`, suppress the diagnostic, or compare the reference before recording
the observed failure. Work on copies if an earlier attempt must be retained.

The three fault classes appear in sequence:

| Stage | Evidence | Question to answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compiler | Format warning treated as an error in `main.c` | Which type does the argument actually have, and which format does that type require? |
| Linker | Missing `duration_to_ticks` definition | Do the declaration, caller, and emitted object symbol have the same name? |
| Sanitizer | Signed multiplication overflows in temperature conversion | Does widening happen before the multiplication or after it? |

Record the diagnostic and its file/line before each repair. Change only the
three marked lines: one output format, one function definition name, and the
temperature multiplication's widening. Keep the supplied conversion rules:
centi-C to centi-F truncates the scaled term toward zero, linear ADC mV rounds
to nearest with halves upward, and timer ticks round upward. Failures preserve
non-null output values; invalid inputs and output overflow are distinct.

## 1. Observe the compiler boundary

From this project directory:

```sh
cd starter
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
```

The initial build must fail. The driver stores the timer product in `uint64_t`
but uses a signed-int format. Read `<inttypes.h>` and the portable `PRIu64`
format macro. A cast that discards upper bits would hide the mismatch rather
than explain the value's type. Repair the marked format and rebuild.

## 2. Inspect the missing definition

The next build must fail at linking. The header and caller request
`duration_to_ticks`; the implementation emits a different name. Inspect the
objects before editing the definition. For the normal CMake Makefile/Ninja
layout, the objects are in `build/CMakeFiles/cse11_tooling_starter.dir/`:

```sh
nm build/CMakeFiles/cse11_tooling_starter.dir/main.c.o
nm build/CMakeFiles/cse11_tooling_starter.dir/engineering_math.c.o
```

`U` marks an undefined reference in the caller, while `T` commonly marks a
definition in the text section. Mach-O output can prefix C symbols with `_`.
Other CMake generators may place objects elsewhere under `build`; inspect the
generated directory rather than guessing a nonexistent path. Reconcile the
marked definition with the public header, then rebuild. Merely having a
declaration does not create a linked definition.

## 3. Reproduce the arithmetic failure with a sanitizer

The ordinary driver now works for its small examples, but that does not prove
the conversion is correct at the boundaries. Use a separate diagnostic build:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build-sanitized -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON
cmake --build build-sanitized
UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 ctest --test-dir build-sanitized --output-on-failure
```

The boundary suite must fail with a signed-integer-overflow diagnostic in the
temperature multiplication. The largest accepted centi-C inputs still require
a product wider than `int32_t`. Casting an overflowing product afterward is
too late. Move the widening to an operand before the multiplication, preserve
the final range check, and rebuild **both** build directories. Pass the normal
and sanitized CTest suites. Do not remove an extreme fixture to make them pass.

## 4. Observe a live call and the built artifact

Use the normal Debug build for debugger work. Debuggers and leak sanitizers
can interfere under process tracing, so use `build`, not `build-sanitized`.
Start `gdb ./build/cse11_tooling_starter`, then enter:

```text
break duration_to_ticks
run
print duration_us
print frequency_hz
next
next
print product
continue
```

The driver passes 1501 microseconds and 1000 Hz; the widened product is
1501000. Step through the source until the declaration has executed before
inspecting that local variable. In LLDB, use
`lldb ./build/cse11_tooling_starter`, `breakpoint set --name duration_to_ticks`,
`run`, `frame variable duration_us frequency_hz`, `next`,
`frame variable product`, and `continue`.

Inspect `nm ./build/cse11_tooling_starter` for the repaired definition, then
use `objdump -d ./build/cse11_tooling_starter` or
`llvm-objdump --disassemble ./build/cse11_tooling_starter`. Identify the
`duration_to_ticks` function in the disassembly. Addresses and instructions
depend on compiler, architecture, and build settings; do not compare fixed
addresses as though they were portable output.

## Completion evidence and walkthrough

The repaired tests report `52 engineering math checks passed`. The driver
exits 0 with:

```text
timer product: 1501000
temperature: -4000 centi-C -> -4000 centi-F
voltage: 512/1023 at 3300 mV -> 1652 mV
timer: 1501 us at 1000 Hz -> 2 ticks
```

Save the original diagnostics, the three marked repairs, passing normal and
sanitized test output, the four-line trace, a debugger observation, and symbol
and disassembly evidence. Explain which tool detects each fault and why the
small driver alone misses the boundary error. An instructor can walk through
prediction, observation, repair, and explanation at each stage; the same
sequence supports independent reading and completion.

`solution` is a separate reference with executable `cse11_tooling_solution`.
Its normal and sanitizer builds pass from the outset. Compare it after saving
the attempt. Optional transfer practice applies this evidence sequence to
another completed course utility; keep it separate from the required repairs.
